description: Canonical operation catalog for generated service operation views and transport bindings.

generated_views.role: HTTP/OpenAPI binding shape aligned to the catalog; not a second operation namespace.
Descriptive operation map and governance notes; excerpt-only unless explicitly marked generated.

registry_rules: New operation_id values MUST be added here before any OpenAPI, HTTP binding table, SDK generator, or alternative transport binding references them.
Generated views MAY change shape, grouping, or field order, but MUST NOT introduce, rename, or remove operation_id values that are absent from this catalog.
Supporting Arkret core does not imply support for every registered operation. Implementations MUST advertise supported_operations and supported_profiles explicitly.

Each surface_groups entry carries a tier (see capability_tiers); only the core tier is implied by claiming v1 protocol support. Extension, interop_bridge, and deployment_local surfaces require explicit advertisement.

Profile matrices in artifacts/profiles/conformance-profiles.json define role-level MUST/SHOULD requirements; the surface groups below define machine-readable capability families for discovery, docs, and lint.
Each operation MUST declare success_shape_kind so SDKs can determine success handling without endpoint-name hard-coding.

Operations with typed OpenAPI bodies SHOULD declare request_schema_ref and/or response_schema_ref. The referenced schema fragment is the source for generated DTO docs and MUST match the OpenAPI component referenced by the HTTP binding.

Operations that still bind OpenAPI request/response bodies to OperationRequest or OperationResult MUST declare generic_binding with request/response booleans, reason, profile_gate, and migration_plan; core-tier operations MUST NOT use generic bindings.

operation_id values MUST end with <kind>.<action>. The kind segment MUST be one of query, stream, resource, command, upload, or exchange; the action segment MUST describe protocol semantics and MUST NOT be an HTTP method name.

resource.replace operations MUST bind to HTTP PUT; resource.delete operations MUST bind to HTTP DELETE; command, upload, exchange, and complex query body operations SHOULD bind to HTTP POST unless their operation notes define a stricter resource URI replacement contract.

Every write operation (kind command/upload/exchange, and resource.replace / resource.delete) MUST declare idempotency_mechanism (one of idempotency_key, object_id, request_id, canonical_hash, protocol_sequence, none) and retry_safe (boolean). Read-only operations (query/stream/resource.get/resource.head) MUST NOT declare these fields.

idempotency_mechanism is the machine-readable source of truth for which idempotency mechanism from api-conventions.md section 6 an operation uses. canonical_hash operations MUST also declare canonical_hash_input as either full_body or an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer. retry_safe=true means a byte-identical full retry of the same request cannot produce duplicate side effects: it returns the original outcome, an equivalent idempotent no-op, or a deterministic conflict. retry_safe=false means blind retries MAY duplicate side effects or consume one-time material; clients MUST NOT retry such operations without out-of-band reconciliation.

capability_tiers.core: Base interoperable surfaces implied by claiming Arkret v1 protocol support (service discovery, identity registry, events/account aggregate).
capability_tiers.extension: Optional interoperable surfaces that are part of the Arkret specification but require explicit discovery/profile advertisement.
capability_tiers.interop_bridge: Adapter surfaces that bridge Arkret to external protocols (MIMI Internet-Drafts, third-party Applet hosts). Implementations advertise these only when the external protocol is supported; bridge operations are not part of any core or extension profile and frequently mirror an in-spec operation via bridges_to.
capability_tiers.deployment_local: Deployment-specific, operator, or product-local surfaces that MUST NOT be assumed from core protocol support alone.

operations.notes: Account Authority exchanges an OIDC authorization code for an opaque, short-lived account_handoff_grant bound to the request DPoP key. The handoff is not ak.session.grant, has no refresh-token semantics, and its closed operation allowlist is issue_identity_binding_challenge, register, and issue_session_grant. It returns bound, identity_creation_active, or identity_creation_busy state and atomically acquires, renews, or fences an identity-creation lease for the authenticated service account. Repeating the same request_id returns the same live outcome. A different holder cannot take an unexpired lease; after expiry, a newly authenticated holder for the same service account may fence it and must preserve any reserved principal_id, operation digest, and public DID-operation checkpoint.

Authenticated by Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus a matching DPoP header. The Account Authority verifies the current lease holder and fence, validates the complete unpublished DID operation, derives principal_id and its canonical operation digest, persists the public operation checkpoint, renews the same-holder lease, and issues a <=300s single-use challenge bound to account, holder cnf.jkt, lease/fence, principal_id, operation digest, audience, origin, trust domain, purpose, and expiry. Repeating the same request_id returns the same unconsumed challenge. Challenge state MUST be shared durable state, not process-local memory.

Canonical account creation/binding operation. In the account-first identity_creation branch the caller MUST present Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus matching DPoP, the current lease/fence, the exact reserved DID inception operation, and a fresh identity-root control proof over the persisted challenge transcript. For did:webvh inception the verifier takes parameters.updateKeys[0] from the operation itself (the root is not a DID Document verificationMethod) and requires verification_key_multibase to match it exactly. The Account Authority CAS-validates account/holder/lease/fence/reservation, consumes the challenge, submits the DID operation internally, accepts only accepted or byte-identical duplicate with a verified head digest, and writes the service-account binding. The (account, principal_id, operation_digest) result is idempotent; published-but-not-yet-bound state is durably completed for that same account and can never be rebound to another account. The operation never accepts recovery words, seed material, or identity-root private keys.

Managed-DID (account-authority) device enrollment, device-lifecycle.md §5.4 / key-management.md §5.0.6. The authenticated session asks its designated enrollment authority to mint a service_attested ak.device.authorize for this session's own device; the authority signs with its persistent enrollment key (never the principal SSK) and returns the full Event. The caller submits it verbatim to POST /_arkret/self/events. Distinct from pair_device (§2.1), which lands an existing-device SAS/QR approval and carries a pairing_code; enroll_device is only the bootstrap / first-device path where no sibling device can approve. The authority MUST require actor_seq=1, a verified identity-creation binding receipt for the same principal/account, and no existing active device; a bare session grant or actor_seq>1 MUST NOT enroll a second long-term device. Later devices use pair_device or the recovery re-anchor strand.

Account Authority single-call session-grant exchange. The response is the client-visible SessionGrantOutcome; any Principal-side local session provisioning is internal. There is no separate client-visible grant-to-bearer exchange step: the client presents ak.session.grant directly to /_arkret/self/* with DPoP (api-conventions §3.3). For proof_kind=oidc_code_exchange, the Account Authority exchanges the authorization code and validates issuer/state/nonce/redirect_uri/principal/device/audience binding. For proof_kind=pre_registration_handoff, the caller instead presents Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus matching DPoP; the handoff's service account MUST already be bound to the requested principal_id. principal_id is required for every proof kind and MUST already have a verified account binding; unknown or unbound returns principal_unknown (404). The Account Authority MUST NOT derive or mint a principal DID from OIDC. A first OIDC interaction may create only the account handoff; the client completes cold-root custody and canonical register before requesting a session grant. For proof_kind=agent_key_proof when high-risk scope needs controller approval, the endpoint returns 403 ErrorEnvelope with error.code=claim_required and closed agent_human_approval_error_details; it never returns CAPTCHA, OTP, password, or browser challenge material to the runtime.

DPoP-bound session-grant rotation (account-lifecycle §4.1, device-lifecycle §3.3). An authorized device presents a DPoP holder proof for the grant's cnf.jkt plus a fresh DID/device proof bound to principal_id, device_id, audience, request_canonical_digest, challenge, issued_at, and expires_at; expires_at - issued_at MUST be <=300s. The old grant is single-use revoked. Account Authority-local op; not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

Account Authority to Auth Server S2S Auth-side logout sub-operation (account-lifecycle §4.1): the Account Authority has already validated the client-visible ak.gate.account.command.logout request, then calls this operation with service-to-service authentication to log out the Auth-side browser/auth session owning the presented ak.session.grant and terminate that session's grant rotation chain. Ordinary clients MUST NOT call this operation; they only call ak.gate.account.command.logout. HTTP-only S2S op; not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

Server-to-server session-grant introspection (RFC 7662-style). The Principal Server validating a presented grant calls this with the grant id or grant_jwt (+ optional audience and optional S2S holder confirmation) and learns whether it is active, plus non-secret grant metadata. The introspection response MUST include the grant's cnf_jkt (RFC 7638 thumbprint of the bound DPoP holder key) so the Principal Server can verify the per-request DPoP proof on /_arkret/self/* (api-conventions §3.3); clients do not send a separate introspection-proof header on self-path requests. session_public_key is also returned for RFC 9421 PoP verification. READ-ONLY: introspection MUST NOT consume/revoke the grant. Authenticated by the configured session_grant_introspection_bearer (server-local); not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

Account Authority ordinary hard logout (account-lifecycle §4.1): single client-visible logout entry. The handler validates the current ak.session.grant + DPoP, terminates the Auth-side auth session / grant rotation chain through ak.gate.account.command.logout_auth_session when Auth-side is split out, and completes or durably schedules the Principal-side local account session + device session cleanup and to-device/push removal. Distinct from revoke_session (targeted session-grant revoke). HTTP-only Account Authority op; not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

Optional Account Authority browser redirect landing / handoff for deployments that use an OIDC redirect URI under /_arkret/gate/account. It MUST NOT issue or return SessionGrantOutcome, ak.session.grant, or Principal local session material; client-visible grant issuance remains ak.gate.account.command.issue_session_grant.

source_signature_anchor.node_to_applet: Source-Service-ID current service DID verification method; Destination-Service-ID MUST equal the Applet registration service_id.
source_signature_anchor.applet_to_arkret_inbound: Applet registration webhook_auth.key_ref; DID part MUST equal Source-Service-ID and the active effective install service_id.

operations.notes: Issues a short-TTL, single-blob, read-only pre-signed URL whose authorization material rides in the URL itself (query string). Used as a deliberate carve-out of the no-credentials-in-URL rule (server-threat-model.md S21) so that browser primitives like /

Enqueues caller-supplied DeviceMessageEnvelope targets into recipient device queues. Each target carries a sender-assigned message_id copied unchanged into the stored envelope; the service deduplicates logical messages by (sender_principal_id, sender_device_id, message_id), returning the existing outcome for identical canonical target content and duplicate_conflict/message_id_conflict for different content. HTTP batch replay is additionally deduplicated by (sender, Idempotency-Key). Queue pruning is only via ak.self.device_messages.command.ack.

Explicit, cumulative, monotonic to-device delivery acknowledgement (client-sync.md §10.1). Queue deletion happens only here; stream cursor advancement (account subscribe after=, device_messages after=) is read-only and MUST NOT prune the queue. Re-acking the same or an older token is a legal no-op. Unknown / expired / cross-bound tokens are rejected with invalid_param (reason invalid_ack_token) without deleting anything.
Writes requester-side ak.contact.requested fact and requester-side consent grants for requested scopes; MUST NOT write target consent or accepted fact.
Target-side accept/reject of a contact request. Accept writes target-controlled consent grants; reject writes no consent.
Holder contact projection from contact facts plus consent-derived directional scopes; account-data contact notes are local decoration only.
Holder-side contact tombstone. Default revocation is limited to contact-managed active consent dots.

Read the authenticated subject's private invite-receive policy. Returns the recommended default when no explicit override is stored; the response is never written into the target Realm durable event log.

Replace the authenticated subject's private invite-receive policy. The body MUST set subject_id equal to the session actor; the override shares the same store as ak.self.contact.command.tombstone(block_peer) blocked_subjects writes.
Idempotent resolver for accepted contacts. Requires accepted contact projection and direct_message consent; create=true creates canonical DM Realm, main Strand, and binding.

Builds a ak.circle.create Operation in the named parent Realm and routes it through the local accept pipeline. Reducer-locked fields (mls_group_ref, state) MUST NOT be actor-supplied; encryption_profile='none' is allowed only when the parent Realm policy floor permits plaintext.
Lists Circles the caller may see within one parent Realm (required realm_id query). Directory visibility is enforced per Circle; non-members of a 'members'-visibility Circle MUST NOT see it.
Reads one Circle projection. Returns not_found when the Circle is invisible to the caller rather than disclosing existence.

Builds ak.circle.member.state. Activating another actor requires ak.circle.member.manage narrowed to this Circle, and the target MUST already be a joined parent-Realm member (strict-subset invariant); a self-join is gated by join_rule.
Builds ak.circle.member.state with membership=leave for the path actor_id.

Rotates the Circle's bound MLS group. MUST NOT acknowledge a rotation without actually changing the cryptographic scope; returns unsupported_feature until the MLS genesis/commit/welcome cascade is wired end-to-end.
Builds ak.circle.archive; transition follows the Circle lifecycle matrix (reducer rejects illegal transitions with circle_not_active).

Builds ak.circle.restore; transition follows the Circle lifecycle matrix (reducer rejects illegal transitions with circle_not_archived). Restore re-enables new writes after pending MLS membership removals are settled.
Builds ak.circle.tombstone (terminal). Response surfaces the terminal state with empty members.

Resource-side appeal against an operator takedown. The appeal packet MUST bind takedown_id, resource id, appellant DID, argument/evidence digest, requested_outcome and created_at, signed by the resource governance key or an authorized advocate; the Directory returns a signed decision receipt. See discovery-directory.md §8.7.

Return one bounded, manifest-committed chunk of a complete_control_state_v1 proof bundle for one authenticated, caller-visible Realm/scope. The request MUST name an exact locally trusted_anchor_seal_id and chunk_index; later chunks pin expected_bundle_digest. The service MUST build from that anchor and return mls_governance_anchor_unreachable instead of substituting another anchor. The service derives membership_frontier and all governance roots from one accepted Seal view; callers cannot supply roots. Responses bind canonical acquisition identity with proof_request_digest, commit all chunks under chunks_root, and use bundle_digest rather than accepted_seal_id as the logical content address. Each response is at most 4 MiB; the logical bundle is at most 256 MiB, 1024 chunks, 4096 Seals, 1048576 covered digests, 262144 control leaves and 128 frontier Events. Exceeding a total bound returns mls_governance_proof_bounds_exceeded with no partial output. Implementations MUST enforce Realm/scope visibility before materialization and MUST fail closed when any covered Event, control state, Seal path, chunk commitment, signature authority, or reducer profile cannot be reconstructed.

HTTP-specific POST/body form of ak.events.query. Semantically identical (same selector / cursor / order / filter / include_completeness parameter set, same response shape including optional range_completeness). Choose when URL length would exceed practical limits (large realms[]/actors[] arrays, complex filters object) or when query parameters would be logged inadvertently by proxies. Non-HTTP transports MUST use the canonical ak.self.events.query.scan binding (SelfEvents/Query / self.events.query.scan), not expose this variant as a separate gRPC or MQ operation.
Dereference a known set of event_id / event_digest references to full EventEnvelope objects. Point lookup by identifier, not a range scan — use ak.self.events.query.scan for selector-based reads.

Long-lived per-Realm / actor event stream with optional bounded catch-up replay. `dropped` and `resync_required` control frames MAY carry `reconnect_after_ms`, a server-directed minimum delay before opening another subscription for the same caller/selector scope; early reconnects are rejected with rate_limited / Retry-After.

Durable self event submission, including ak.invite.claim. For ak.invite.claim, the receiving Realm reducer is the authoritative state machine: it MUST match token_commitment, re-check verification_service_id allowlist against current Realm policy, reject claim_nonce replay, perform pending -> claimed / membership-proposal effects, and run expiry cleanup before accepting.

Submit a client-signed Seal. Except for the canonical genesis exception, the signature MUST satisfy the predecessor governance state's ak.component.notary.v1 membership and threshold rules; Realm visibility or device ownership is insufficient. The receiver recomputes the Seal id, recursive coverage, completeness_root, state_root, signer authority and signature.
Federation peer Events surface describe. This endpoint describes the server-to-server peer event bindings; it is not a client self/events binding.

Federation peer frontier probe. Requires service-to-service authentication, Source/Destination service DID headers, trust-domain headers, and Realm federation_peer authorization. It returns the federation peer frontier response shape on the dedicated peer trust surface.

Federation peer pull/backfill query. Uses the same selector, cursor, order, and response semantics as ak.self.events.query.scan, but the HTTP trust surface is peer and the caller MUST be an authorized federation peer service.

HTTP-specific POST/body form of ak.peer.events.query.scan. Semantically identical to GET /_arkret/peer/events; use it when federation selectors or filters are too large or sensitive for query strings.

Federation peer event reference resolution for missing prev_refs / causal references. Requires authorized federation peer service authentication and applies the same reference-disclosure and history-visibility rules as peer event query.

Federation peer event push. Body is EventsSubmitFederationRequestBody and the caller MUST use service-to-service authentication with Source/Destination service DID and trust-domain headers. Federated ak.invite.claim events are still decided by the destination Realm reducer, which MUST enforce token_commitment, current allowlist re-check, claim_nonce replay rejection, membership proposal conversion, and expiry cleanup; peer ingress prechecks are not state authority.

Private Principal Server to Principal Server invite delivery. Requires service-to-service authentication, Destination-Service-ID equal to invite_address.recipient_service_id, a ak.invite.create event whose invitee equals invite_address.subject_id, and introduction_evidence accepted by the recipient invite_receive_policy.

Private Principal Server to Principal Server contact fact delivery. Requires service-to-service authentication, Destination-Service-ID equal to contact_address.recipient_service_id, and a signed ak.contact.* envelope the recipient projects into the target holder's contact projection without re-signing.
Federation peer snapshot manifest head for snapshot-assisted bootstrap. Requires service-to-service authentication and Realm federation_peer authorization.

Canonical broadcast ephemeral send operation for ak.schema.ephemeral_envelope.v1. Carries ak.presence, ak.typing, ak.receipt.read, and ak.call.signal; MUST NOT persist the signal as a durable Event or advance actor_seq / Realm frontier.

Media service token exchange operation. Issues a short-lived (TTL <= 600s) backend_token + participant_binding for joining a focus declared in ak.realm.media_service.foci[]. Same wire across all backend types (livekit / mediasoup / janus / arkret-native); only backend_token shape is type-specific. Token issuer DID MUST be one of the Realm-authorized media service DIDs; clients reject otherwise (token_issuer_unauthorised). See zh/crypto-media/media-service-binding.md §3.

The wrapper carries one complete DID method-native operation. did_method is the bare method discriminator and MUST equal the DID method component. Controller/update/recovery authorization comes only from the native operation; transport authentication is admission-only. Unsupported methods, generic replace/patch/document fallbacks, stale heads, and sibling forks fail closed. Exact canonical-operation retries are duplicate-success without a second history append.

Idempotently return or create the service DID bound to the canonical (service_type, public_base) registration key. The client supplies and controls a signed did:webvh inception operation; the Provider verifies the proof and endpoint binding and never receives private key material. Provider persistence MUST enforce UNIQUE(service_type, public_base) and MUST reject an existing hosted document that declares the same key even when the mapping row is absent.
Read the service registration bound to the canonical (service_type, public_base) key without creating or mutating identity state.

Read the currently accepted ak.schema.recovery_policy.v1 projection for the authenticated or explicitly selected principal. Returns active_policy=null when no accepted policy exists; does not publish, rotate, or revoke policy state.

Publish a signed ak.schema.recovery_policy.v1 genesis policy or rotation for the authenticated principal. HTTP binding is POST because the principal/authority is derived from authenticated proof and signed policy state rather than a URI-addressed resource slot. Servers MUST verify auth_data.signed_fields, signature authority, version monotonicity, and supersedes linkage before accepting.

Resolves a short-lived agent pairing token carried out-of-band, usually as a URL fragment in a QR/link. The pairing token MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; the response is the six-field agent_pairing_bootstrap.

Runtime-to-controller pending approval request for native personal-agent key pairing. The runtime proves possession of the local key and the short pairing code; the controller still must approve by signing ak.agent.key.authorize. The pairing code and proof-of-possession MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string. One open pairing_request_id has at most one pending stable ak.agent.runtime_key_binding.v1 digest: same-binding retries retain approval/notification ids and update freshness proof, while a different binding fails with HTTP 409 agent_runtime_request_conflict without replacement.

Runtime-side poll for the controller decision on a previously submitted runtime key request. The pairing_request_id + pairing_code + agent_id triple is the query credential and MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; a record miss and a pairing_code or agent_id mismatch MUST be indistinguishable (both not_found). Once approved, the outcome carries authorized_event_ref plus the authorized key binding; the runtime MUST compare authorized_public_key_digest against its own key and treat a mismatch as paired-by-another-runtime. HTTP responses MUST carry Retry-After; clients wait at least that interval and use 1s/2s/5s/10s then at most 30s backoff, stopping after pairing expiry.

Resolves an online invite locator token carried out-of-band, usually as a URL fragment in a QR/link. The locator token MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; the response is a signed principal_locator.
Canonical HTTP binding is POST /_arkret/self/policy/check. Paths carry no version segment; protocol version is negotiated via *.describe / supported_operations (see sync/api-conventions.md).
Lists typed cross-Realm links projected from ak.realm.link. direction is outbound/inbound/both; link_kind_allow is a comma-separated allowlist of canonical link kinds.

Builds an ak.realm.link Control Move from realm_id -> target_realm_id. General directed cycles are valid and traversal uses a visited set; admission rejects only self-reference, invalid kind, invalid payload, or an illegal FSM transition. Self-reference returns schema_violation with reason_code realm_link_self_reference; an illegal transition returns failed_precondition with reason_code realm_link_invalid_transition.

Writes a tombstoning ak.realm.link Move (status=tombstoned) for the (realm_id, target_realm_id, link_kind) triple. link_kind defaults to governed_by; callers may override via the link_kind query param.

Returns the merged effective policy after walking governed_by / inherits_policy_from ancestors per the Realm's ak.realm.inheritance_policy. inheritance_mode=none when no inheritance policy is projected (implicit inheritance is forbidden).

Returns the projected ak.realm.organization relationship statements for the Realm (active / revoked / expired, latest-per-(organization_id, relationship)) plus declared owning_organizations hints with no verified statement. The caller must be authorized to read the Realm. A relationship is only verified when lifecycle_phase=verified_active; declared_organization_hints are unverified claims and MUST NOT be rendered as official / governed / endorsed.
Reads the projected ak.realm.policy_server config. Returns not_found when neither the Realm nor its governed_by ancestor chain declared one. from_org_fallback=true marks an inherited config.

Builds a ak.realm.policy_server Move (admission capability ak.policy.manage). Reducer validates URL scheme and on_timeout enum. This admin DTO is a simplified projection of the canonical payload (server_id/endpoint/public_keys/applies_to/fail_mode).
Tombstones the per-Realm ak.realm.policy_server cell so callers fall back to the governed_by chain or local-only capability check. Empty success response.
Reads the Realm lifecycle projection (owner + members + deleted). Returns not_found when the Realm is invisible to the caller.

Builds a ak.realm.archive Move. The archived facet changes when the lifecycle event is accepted into the Realm event log; archived=false clears the archived facet unless a terminal lifecycle state already applies.

Builds a ak.realm.freeze Move. The frozen facet changes when the lifecycle event is accepted into the Realm event log; frozen=true rejects ordinary non-exempt writes with realm_frozen and frozen=false clears the freeze facet unless a terminal lifecycle state already applies.

Builds a terminal ak.realm.tombstone Move with a successor_realm_id. The tombstoned state changes when the lifecycle event is accepted into the Realm event log; later ordinary writes fail with realm_terminal_state.
Builds a terminal ak.realm.destroy Move. The destroyed state changes when the lifecycle event is accepted into the Realm event log; later ordinary writes fail with realm_terminal_state.
Full event-log + operation dump for a Realm (schema ak.export.realm.v1). Caller must be authorized to read the Realm; payload visibility still follows Realm policy.
Returns the organization-inherited effective moderation policy view: inheritance chain, organization policy layers, the Realm's own override, and merged effective rules.

Writes a Realm moderation-policy override (ak.realm.moderation_policy). Only the Realm owner may write; an override that loosens an action an organization policy denies requires explicit organization approval embedded in the document, otherwise the server returns failed_precondition with reason_code=requires_organization_approval.
Lists holder-private consent cells for the authenticated holder only. Peer actors MUST NOT receive cell state, dots, expiry or request timestamps.
Reads one holder-private consent cell. The authenticated actor MUST equal holder_did or be an explicitly authorised holder controller; peers never receive this DTO.
Builds a ak.consent.grant Control Move on the holder's consent cell. The authenticated actor MUST be authorized to write the holder's consent (holder or an explicitly authorized controller/agent).

Builds a ak.consent.revoke Control Move enumerating the active grant dots for the (consent_id, peer, consent_scope). Revoking consent_scope=any cascades all concrete scopes; revoking a concrete scope leaves others intact.

Submits an opaque consent-contact request from the authenticated peer. peer_did defaults to and MUST equal the actor. The response is identical for missing holders, policy denial, rate limiting, silent drop and quarantine acceptance; the operation never returns a consent cell.
Lists the authenticated actor's account_data entries. content is stored verbatim and is opaque to the server.
Reads one account_data entry by data_type key. Returns not_found when the key is unset.

Builds a ak.account_data.set actor-private write. Controller-private registered types reject agent / applet / service principals. content is stored verbatim; clients own canonical encoding and (for sensitive keys) client-side encryption.
Deletes one account_data entry and fans out an actor-private update to the holder's other devices.

Builds a ak.read_cursor.advance actor-private write for (actor_id, realm_id, read_scope, position). Multi-device convergence is by HLC max with device_id tiebreak; the cursor is never published into shared Realm history.
Lists the authenticated actor's read markers, optionally filtered by the realm_id query param.
Extension read surface listing reducer-maintained Strand lifecycle rows for a Realm. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.
Extension read surface listing reducer-maintained Morph lifecycle rows for a Realm. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.
Extension read surface listing reducer-maintained Space lifecycle rows for a Realm. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.

Optional extension read surface that materializes a View{kind=collection} projection such as board/list/table/calendar. The response is a derived read model computed from signed Events, reducer profile, View definition, and the returned frontier; it is not a canonical truth source.

Optional extension read surface returning the authorized document body, version, relation, comment, and cursor-presence read-model for a single document Morph addressed within its Realm. Canonical truth remains the Morph/Relation/Message event history.

Holder-bound one-shot read of the current principal account projection. Returns principal_id, account lifecycle state, device summaries, optional ActorProfile, and signed handle-claim evidence or refs. It MUST NOT return an unsigned bare handle as authoritative identity. Naming: the trailing segment 'viewer' is intentionally outside the api-conventions.md §2.4 read-verb taxonomy; it follows the GraphQL 'viewer' convention (the authenticated subject's own projection). The target is located by the holder-bound session rather than an external id, so 'get' does not apply, and 'viewer' (subject identity projection) stays distinct from 'describe' (service capability metadata).

Holder-bound service wrapper around ak.profile.update / Actor Profile projection. Request body is a closed patch over display_name, avatar_blob_ref, and profile_fields.<key>; profile_fields.bio is the canonical personal bio field and avatar_url is not accepted on the Arkret protocol path.

Streaming push of cross-Realm account-aggregate deltas (cross-Realm frontier, to_device queue, account_data, device_lists, presence, unread / notification counts). Connection is long-lived; server pushes NDJSON frames as new data becomes available. Symmetric with ak.self.events.stream.subscribe — both are streaming subscriptions, differing only in scope (self.events.stream.subscribe = per-Realm event log; self.account.stream.subscribe = account-aggregate). `dropped` and `resync_required` control frames MAY carry `reconnect_after_ms`, a server-directed minimum delay before opening another subscription for the same principal/device/filter scope; early reconnects are rejected with rate_limited / Retry-After. Presence changes are sent through ak.self.ephemeral.command.send, not this read-only stream subscription.

High-assurance optional endpoint to revoke a previously issued cursor authority. Revocation hits return cursor_revoked and MUST NOT advance account subscribe position, barrier wait, or dropped recovery state. To-device queue deletion is decoupled from cursors entirely and happens only via ak.self.device_messages.command.ack.
